scientific_scope: Independent-source candidates for the exact-temperature diagnostic required after NASA-EXTERNAL-001. Registry inclusion is not scientific admissibility.

candidates.title: Comprehensive battery aging dataset: capacity and impedance fade measurements of a lithium-ion NMC/C-SiO cell - version 2 result data
known_data_quality_events: Temperature-control deviation from 2022-11-27 22:40 UTC to 2022-11-29 16:50 UTC affected all four pools; measured temperatures must be retained and handled explicitly.
A 25 degree_Celsius pool Peltier circuit failed on 2023-04-23 around 11:47, lowering average cell temperature by about 2.5 degree_Celsius and increasing within-pool variation.
Cell surface temperature may deviate from pool setpoint during operation, especially for severely aged fast-charging cold cells.
source_notes: The publication reports 228 cells across 76 operating conditions, including 48 cyclic-aging conditions and four operating temperatures.

Protocol-temperature mismatch: the NASA diagnostic field ambient_temperature_median_c is the battery-level median of source-recorded ambient_temperature on NASA discharge operations, while KIT moves cells from their 0-40 degree_Celsius aging operating temperature to 25 degree_Celsius before the standardized capacity check. KIT aging temperature therefore cannot be substituted for the NASA capacity-measurement ambient field, and the KIT capacity-measurement temperature itself is fixed at 25 degree_Celsius.

Exact-horizon mismatch: NASA forecasting requires a target row exactly at discharge-operation ordinal origin_cycle + horizon with no interpolation; KIT comparison capacity is collected in scheduled check-ups (first follow-up after one week and subsequent check-ups at three-week intervals) and represented over check-up/EFC progression.

Target/reference mismatch: the current NASA public importer derives capacity_retention_percent from each source discharge Capacity divided by the documented 2.0 Ah rated capacity, whereas KIT remaining usable capacity is measured during a standardized 25 degree_Celsius, 1/3 C full CC-CV check-up procedure.

Authoritative KIT semantics are documented in Luh and Blank, Scientific Data 11, 1004 (2024), DOI 10.1038/s41597-024-03831-x. NASA target and protocol semantics are enforced by src/platform_core/battery_intelligence/nasa_pcoe.py, src/platform_core/battery_intelligence/nasa_pcoe_rated.py, and the fixed-horizon Battery Degradation Intelligence contract.
This source remains scientifically valuable as an independent battery-aging benchmark candidate, but it is not admissible as direct evidence for the current NASA exact-horizon external diagnostic.
This source must remain an independent source cohort and may not be pooled with NASA batteries merely because temperatures are similar.
